review_notes:
I read all of WedgeKGeneralConverse.lean. It has two theorems. The second one only splits the iff and calls the first theorem and an existing lemma, so it has no repeated reasoning of its own. The first theorem is a linear chain of API applications and contains nothing duplicated internally.

I searched related files for repeated proofs. The setup "graph_connected_vertexWedge ... hG.connected hH.connected" plus "rw [genus_vertexWedge, hG.genus_one, hH.genus_one]; norm_num" appears in about seven wedge files. These include WedgeKGeneralSymmetric.lean (lines 99-104), OppositeWedgeKGeneralClassification.lean (lines 38-46) and TwoVertexWedgeSubmodularity.lean. Each copy is 3-5 lines of routine rewriting with existing lemmas (`genus_vertexWedge`, `graph_connected_vertexWedge`, `wedgeRightVertex_unmarked`).

A helper such as "PointedGenusOneRigid pair gives a genus-2 connected wedge" would only shorten those copies. Under the rubric this is a short calculation or routine unfolding, not nontrivial repeated mathematical reasoning. The larger swap and rigidity argument in WedgeKGeneralSymmetric.lean (lines 83-136) occurs once, and the target file does not repeat it. I therefore found no justified finding. The only uncertainty is that I did not read every wedge file in full.
